432	def min_backtest_length(sr, n_trials, sr_var_trials):
433	    """Sessions needed for the observed per-session Sharpe to clear the expected maximum of n_trials (AFML 14.7)."""
434	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
435	    sr0 = math.sqrt(sr_var_trials) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
436	    return round(float((sr0 / sr) ** 2 + 1), 1) if sr > 0 else None

439	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- resampling: stationary block bootstrap of sessions, SPA
440	def stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, mean_block=BOOT_MEAN_BLOCK, seed=SEED, tag=""):
441	    """Politis & Romano stationary bootstrap indices (draws x T_) over T_ ordered sessions; seeded and reproducible."""
442	    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(_sha(f"{seed}|boot|{tag}"), 16) % (2 ** 32))
443	    p = 1.0 / mean_block
444	    starts = rng.integers(0, T_, size=(draws, T_)); cont = rng.random((draws, T_)) >= p
445	    idx = np.empty((draws, T_), dtype=int)
446	    idx[:, 0] = starts[:, 0]
447	    for t_ in range(1, T_):
448	        idx[:, t_] = np.where(cont[:, t_], (idx[:, t_ - 1] + 1) % T_, starts[:, t_])
449	    return idx

454	    T_ = len(vec["sessions"]); idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
455	    ks, kn, ss, sn = (vec[k][idx].sum(axis=1) for k in ("kept_sum", "kept_n", "skipped_sum", "skipped_n"))

459	    q = lambda v: [round(float(np.nanquantile(v, a)), 2), round(float(np.nanquantile(v, 1 - a)), 2)]
460	    return dict(draws=draws, ci=ci, diff_ci=q(d), kept_mean_ci=q(km), diff_p_le0=round(float(np.nanmean(d <= 0)), 4),

464	def selection_gain(vec):
465	    """Per-session selection gain d_t = kept mean in session t minus the session's mean over all units (0 when nothing kept):
466	    the per-session statistic behind the session-matched random control (its expectation under random selection is 0)."""
467	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
468	        km = np.where(vec["kept_n"] > 0, vec["kept_sum"] / vec["kept_n"], np.nan)
469	        am = vec["all_sum"] / vec["all_n"]

474	def spa(vectors, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, tag=""):
475	    """White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA over a family of candidates: H0 = no candidate has positive expected selection
476	    gain (per-session kept mean minus the session mean). Stationary bootstrap of sessions, studentised statistics, Hansen's
477	    consistent recentring. Returns the best candidate's statistic and the RC / SPA p-values."""
478	    Dm = np.array([selection_gain(v)[0] for v in vectors], dtype=float)       # M x T
479	    M, T_ = Dm.shape
480	    mu = Dm.mean(axis=1); se = Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) / math.sqrt(T_); se = np.where(se > 0, se, np.inf)
481	    tstat = np.sqrt(T_) * mu / (Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) + 1e-12)
482	    idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
483	    best = int(np.argmax(tstat)); rc_stat = float(tstat[best])
484	    # bootstrap of the max studentised statistic under the recentred null
485	    mub = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].mean(axis=1) for d in range(draws)])           # draws x M
486	    sdb = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].std(axis=1, ddof=1) for d in range(draws)]) + 1e-12
487	    rc_max = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu) / sdb, axis=1)                       # White: recentre at the sample mean
488	    thr = np.sqrt(np.var(Dm, axis=1, ddof=1) / T_ * 2 * math.log(math.log(T_)))
489	    mu_c = np.where(mu < -thr, mu, 0.0)                                            # Hansen's consistent recentring
490	    spa_max = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c) / sdb, axis=1)
491	    return dict(candidates=M, sessions=T_, best=best, best_mean_gain=round(float(mu[best]), 2), best_t=round(rc_stat, 3),
492	                rc_p=round(float((rc_max >= rc_stat).mean()), 4), spa_p=round(float((spa_max >= rc_stat).mean()), 4), draws=draws)

495	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- structural breaks of the book's own expectancy
496	def _hac_var(x, lag=5):
497	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float) - np.mean(x); T_ = len(x)
498	    s = float((x * x).sum())
499	    for k in range(1, lag + 1):
500	        w = 1 - k / (lag + 1); s += 2 * w * float((x[k:] * x[:-k]).sum())
501	    return s / T_ / T_                                                             # variance of the mean

504	def chow_mean(x, y, lag=5):
505	    """HAC (Newey-West, Bartlett, lag 5) t-test of a difference of means between two consecutive segments."""
506	    x, y = np.asarray(x, dtype=float), np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
507	    if len(x) < 5 or len(y) < 5: return dict(t=None, p=None, n=[len(x), len(y)])
508	    t_ = (y.mean() - x.mean()) / math.sqrt(_hac_var(x, lag) + _hac_var(y, lag))
509	    return dict(t=round(float(t_), 3), p=round(float(2 * (1 - sst.norm.cdf(abs(t_)))), 4), mean_before=round(float(x.mean()), 2),
510	                mean_after=round(float(y.mean()), 2), n=[len(x), len(y)])
511

513	def bde_cusum(x, k=10):
514	    """Brown-Durbin-Evans CUSUM of recursive residuals of the constant-mean model on the ordered series x: the maximum
515	    crossing of the 5% bands +-0.948 sqrt(T-k) (1 + 2 (r-k)/(T-k)); reports whether the path leaves the band and where."""
516	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
517	    if T_ <= k + 2: return dict(break_detected=None)
518	    w = np.array([(x[t_] - x[:t_].mean()) / math.sqrt(1 + 1 / t_) for t_ in range(k, T_)])
519	    sig = w.std(ddof=1)
520	    W = np.cumsum(w) / sig
521	    r = np.arange(k + 1, T_ + 1)
522	    band = 0.948 * math.sqrt(T_ - k) * (1 + 2 * (r - k) / (T_ - k))
523	    ex = np.abs(W) > band
524	    return dict(break_detected=bool(ex.any()), first_crossing_index=int(np.argmax(ex)) + k if ex.any() else None,
525	                max_ratio=round(float(np.max(np.abs(W) / band)), 3), T=T_)
526

528	def break_tests(T, lag=5):
529	    """The pre-registration step: has the book's per-session expectancy (active sessions, label L1) changed inside IS or at the
530	    IS / OOS boundary? Rolling 60-session mean with block-bootstrap bands, BDE CUSUM, HAC Chow tests per calendar year, and the
531	    one permitted OOS aggregate read: the Chow test at 2026-01-01 (it decides the OOS caveat, never a key)."""
532	    rows = np.arange(T.n)
533	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]
534	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist()))); idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
535	    per = np.bincount(idx, weights=net, minlength=len(S)) / np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(S))
536	    day = dict(zip(T.session, T.day)); days = np.array([day[int(s)] for s in S])
537	    is_ = days <= IS_END
538	    x_is = per[is_]
539	    years = sorted({d[:4] for d in days[is_]})
540	    chow_years = {}
541	    for y in years[1:]:
542	        before = x_is[np.array([d[:4] < y for d in days[is_]])]; after = x_is[np.array([d[:4] == y for d in days[is_]])]
543	        chow_years[y] = chow_mean(before, after, lag)
544	    boundary = chow_mean(x_is, per[~is_], lag)
545	    roll = pd.Series(x_is).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy()
546	    idxb = stationary_bootstrap_idx(len(x_is), 500, tag="roll")
547	    rb = np.array([pd.Series(x_is[idxb[d]]).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy() for d in range(500)])
548	    lo, hi = np.nanquantile(rb, 0.05, axis=0), np.nanquantile(rb, 0.95, axis=0)
549	    outside = int(np.nansum((roll < lo) | (roll > hi)))
550	    return dict(label=T.label, active_is_sessions=int(is_.sum()), is_mean_per_session=round(float(x_is.mean()), 2),

553	                winners_only_boundary=chow_mean(x_is[x_is > 0], per[~is_][per[~is_] > 0], lag) if (per[~is_] > 0).sum() >= 5 else None,
554	                caveat=("IS/OOS boundary Chow p < 0.05: the OOS window is not from the same process; every OOS table carries this"
555	                        if boundary["p"] is not None and boundary["p"] < 0.05 else "no boundary break at 5%"))

559	def go_no_go(res, tf, cpcv=None, pbo_value=None, dsr=None, spa_p=None, boot=None):
560	    """The pre-registered pass rule on a candidate's IS results. Returns (passed, {check: (ok, value)})."""
561	    ch = {}
562	    ch["kept_share>=20%"] = (res.get("kept_share") is not None and res["kept_share"] >= GO["kept_share_min"], res.get("kept_share"))
563	    ch[f"kept_n>={GO['kept_n_min'][tf]}"] = (res.get("kept_n", 0) >= GO["kept_n_min"][tf], res.get("kept_n"))
564	    ch["diff>0"] = (res.get("diff") is not None and res["diff"] > 0, res.get("diff"))
565	    ch["diff_top1_removed>0"] = (res.get("diff_top1_removed") is not None and res["diff_top1_removed"] > GO["top1_removed_diff_min"], res.get("diff_top1_removed"))
566	    ch["kept_mean_slip8>0"] = (res.get("kept_mean_slip8") is not None and res["kept_mean_slip8"] > GO["slip8_kept_mean_min"], res.get("kept_mean_slip8"))
567	    ch[f"sign_blocks>={GO['sign_blocks_min']}/12"] = (res.get("sign_blocks") is not None and res["sign_blocks"] >= GO["sign_blocks_min"], res.get("sign_blocks"))
568	    ch["control_pct>=95"] = (res.get("control_pct") is not None and res["control_pct"] >= GO["control_pct_min"], res.get("control_pct"))
569	    if cpcv is not None: ch["cpcv_p5_diff>0"] = (cpcv.get("diff_p5") is not None and cpcv["diff_p5"] > GO["cpcv_p5_diff_min"], cpcv.get("diff_p5"))
570	    if pbo_value is not None: ch["pbo<=0.2"] = (pbo_value <= GO["pbo_max"], pbo_value)
571	    if dsr is not None: ch["dsr_p<0.1"] = (dsr.get("p") is not None and dsr["p"] < GO["dsr_p_max"], dsr.get("p"))
572	    if spa_p is not None: ch["spa_p<=0.10"] = (spa_p <= GO["spa_p_max"], spa_p)
573	    if boot is not None: ch["boot_ci_excludes_0"] = (boot["diff_ci"][0] > 0, boot["diff_ci"])
574	    return all(v[0] for v in ch.values()), ch

1	# Extended as-of features (`fz_v3/out/features_ext/<tf>/ext_features.parquet`)
2	
3	Built by `studies/ext_features/build_ext.py` (kernels in `ext_lib.py`), verified by `finalize.py` on the truncated tape, documented by `write_docs.py`.
4	One row per Foundation SETUP of `data/<tf>/features.parquet`, keyed by `setup_i` (join on it; the label and the split come from the base table through `harness.load`).
5	These columns are candidate features for the importance study (DESIGN_PANEL: quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, both judges) and nowhere else: no gate was searched here, no label was read.
6	
7	Rows: minute 5326 SETUPs (5266 L1 units), 5minute 1012 SETUPs (1002 L1 units). Columns: 61 per timeframe (identical names on both).
8	
9	## Conventions
10	
11	- **as-of**: every value at SETUP bar `k` is a function of bars `<= k` (the SETUP bar included) and, for the fitted families, of a model frozen on the fit window.
12	- **fit window** = the IS bars of sessions 2021-10-01 .. 2023-09-30, the first IS half (489 sessions; 182,557 bars on 1m, 36,514 on 5m). Every z-scoring statistic, mixture, HMM, jump-model centroid and lambda, BOCPD standardisation and the FFD d* is estimated there and nowhere else: unsupervised, label-free; the second IS half and OOS never enter a fit. Inference is a forward pass over the whole tape from bar 0 with the frozen model. For bars inside the fit window the frozen statistics are, by construction, in-sample (a label-free in-sample effect, stated here; the truncation check below cannot see it because the cut is after the fit window).
13	- **gap-free log return**: `log(close_t / close_{t-1})`, except at a session's first bar where it is `log(close_t / open_t)`, so the overnight gap never enters a return-based statistic (the base README's window convention). FFD and BSADF work on the log close level itself and therefore see the gap as a level step (causal, stated).
14	- **same-session window**: cut at the session's first bar `s0 = k - session_bar`.
15	- **state relabelling**: for every GMM / HMM / jump model the states are ordered by ascending mean `(high-low)/atr14` so that state 0 is the quietest; the tables below give the means in original units.
16	- **truncation check**: the same builder ran on `data/<tf>/trunc_20250630_120000/` (bars up to 2025-06-30 12:00, same fit window) and every column was compared for every SETUP before the cut at tolerance 1e-9 (NaN pattern included); a differing column is dropped. Result below.

1	# ext_features: FINDINGS
2	
3	**What this study is.** The extended as-of scalar features the design panel hands to the importance study (quant-ml-canon-feature-importance; regime-breaks and regime-states judges: features only; motif-shapelet judges: the two novelty scalars only; rocket-probe judges: the three window scalars only; vision-labels Judge 1: hindsight proxies are labels and are not computed). No gate search, no threshold, no ledger row: `ledger_families = []`. The only label-side read is the row count through `harness.load`. Definitions were fixed in `build_ext.py` before any output was looked at; they are repeated column by column in `features_ext/README.md`.

5	## Definitions (fixed before the numbers)
6	
7	See `features_ext/README.md`, section *Columns* (definition, causal argument, fit-window statement per column). content.subject: Validation harness: splitter (12 IS blocks, purge by label exit, 3-session embargo), CPCV paths, append-only ledger via score(), PBO, DSR, block bootstrap, SPA
content.description: fz_v3/out/harness.py: the single evaluator. Every gate candidate goes through score(); kept-vs-skipped expectancy, session-matched random control (fz_report.random_control), permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p), CPCV 11 paths, go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV p5 diff > 0, DSR p < 0.1, kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300/80, top-1%-removed value > 0, slippage 8 pts survival). Break tests (BDE CUSUM, Chow) as pre-registration.

content.subject: Feature vocabulary pass: clustered MDA/MDI/SFI, FFD, BSADF/CUSUM, BOCPD run length, novelty scalars, SHAP interactions; freeze <= 8 clusters

content.subject: H1-H5 classical studies through the harness (gate audit, regime, volume, levels, learned gate) on IS

content.subject: Learned-gate family: meta-labelling + full-information policy tree, distilled to rule list / scorecard; regime states; LLM hypotheses (round 0 blind, round 1 cross-fitted); FQI exit; session stop; conformal operating point; sizing
content.description: DESIGN_PANEL merged program: meta-label gate (L1 label, winsorised |net| weights, HGB/bagging ceilings, scorecard, rule list), policy trees, GMM/HMM/BOCPD regime states, LLM-hypothesis rounds with family-wise max-T permutation, FQI exit policy (learner C grid, B hindsight imitation, A FQI), session stop rule with within-session x hour null, conformal skip operating point, sizing conditional on a surviving gate, null tapes (5m), adversarial drift.
content.activeForm: Running the learned-gate family and modern-ML studies

content.subject: Walk-forward learn-after-each-trade policy with the trade journal (IS learning curve, continued through OOS); compose with rl.py for exit/size
content.description: fz_learn.py prototype: journal rows per SETUP (features, decision, reason, model state id, fill, exit, MFE/MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R, running equity/DD/PF); online learners (LinUCB/Thompson on logistic or tree-embedded model, online GBM refits, k-trade cadence); fractional Kelly sizing with max lots and daily loss stop; learning curve vs take-all and random control; deterministic replay.

content.description: fz_v3/out/oos_once.py reads frozen candidate JSON + sha; scores OOS 2026-01-01..2026-09-25 with random control, permutation p, kept-vs-skipped, winner recall; the learner continues updating through OOS as it would live. 216	### quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate (priority 2)
217	
218	**technique.** Meta-labelling: a secondary model over the Foundation primary model, trained on triple-barrier and intraday label variants with return-attribution (|net|) sample weights, uniqueness weights where labels overlap, optional time decay; bagged depth-limited trees and a depth-3 interaction-constrained gradient booster as ceilings, a binned logistic scorecard as the deployable form, distilled to a rule list of at most 8 depth-3 rules.
219	
220	**what_it_answers.** Given that Foundation already chose side and entry, what is P(the trade pays after costs | as-of context) at the SETUP bar, which SETUPs should be skipped, and does a gate trained to preserve the large winners (the user's 'avoid only loss trades') beat the frozen ST7/ST8 rooms gate and the session-matched random control on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, on IS out-of-fold and once on OOS? Also: which label (engine, intraday, symmetric barrier, trend-scanning) yields the most robust gate.
221	
222	**method.** Inputs: features.parquet per timeframe through an allowlist of as-of columns (97 numeric plus one-hot or count encodings of fz_read, fz_gate, fz_block_reason, fz_branch, dir, hv3_dir, card_out_side, last_bos_dir, last_choch_dir, last6_kinds); bars.parquet to recompute labels. Labels, all from bars after the SETUP bar: L0 = the engine net as built (multi-session holds); L1 = Foundation intraday: the same stop / next-CHoCH exit but forced out at the close of the entry session's last bar opening at or before 15:25, priced as the lab does (lab.trade_charges ZERODHA_NFO_FUT on slipped prices, 5 pts per side, lot 65); L2 = symmetric triple barrier: lower barrier = the Foundation stop, upper barrier = entry + 1 x stop distance (and 2 x as a variant), vertical = 15:25, first-touch with the engine's same-bar conventions (stop first, a session's first candle fills at its close); L3 = trend-scanning: for horizons 5..60 bars the t-value of the OLS slope of close after the SETUP, label = sign and |t| at the horizon of maximum |t| relative to dir (the 'large move' the user describes). Primary training label = L1 binary (net > 0); L0/L2/L3 are robustness labels, every gate is evaluated on L1 because that is the book ST13/ST14 will trade (square_off 15:25). Weights: w_i proportional to |net_i| (return attribution), normalised to sum n; class balance by reweighting the 22% winners; time decay c in {1, 0.5} as a sensitivity (study 6 decides whether it is needed); average uniqueness computed from the concurrency of label lifetimes (expected 1.0 for L0/L1 since no Foundation trades overlap; below 1 for L2/L3 with vertical barriers) and used as BaggingClassifier max_samples. Models: (a) BaggingClassifier of DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth 3-5, min_weight_fraction_leaf 0.05, class_weight balanced), 300 estimators; (b) HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_depth 3, max_iter <= 200, learning_rate 0.05, l2_regularization, interaction_cst = the feature clusters from the importance study, monotonic_cst where the hypothesis states a direction); (c) binned logistic scorecard: KBinsDiscretizer (quantile, 4-6 bins) on at most 12 shortlisted features, L1-penalised LogisticRegression, coefficients rounded to integer points. Protocol: the harness splitter (12 blocks, purge by L-specific exit bar, 3-session embargo), nested choice of the skip threshold tau in {0.10, ..., 0.40} inside each training fold by maximising kept expectancy subject to |net|-weighted winner recall >= 0.90; OOF probabilities saved per model and label (consumed by the conformal and sizing studies). IS-OOF evaluation per model: kept net, skipped net, kept-vs-skipped mean difference and permutation p, precision/recall on losers, share of top-decile winners skipped, control percentile from fz_report.random_control on the kept positions per session, CPCV path distribution. Distillation: fit a depth-3 tree and a greedy rule list (<= 8 conjunctive rules, depth <= 3, features from the importance shortlist, thresholds at quantile grid points) to the OOF decision p_win >= tau (not to the labels), report fidelity, re-run the full evaluation with the rule list alone; log every distillation trial in the harness ledger. Freeze: the rule-list JSON, the scorecard JSON and tau with sha, before OOS. OOS once: the frozen rule list, the frozen scorecard, the frozen ST7/ST8 gate and raw Foundation, same table. Also state explicitly why RL is not used: one-step decision, counterfactual observed for every SETUP, no overlap.

Labels are recomputed from bars strictly after setup_i and stored in a separate file. Purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, thresholds chosen inside training folds only, OOF predictions never reused for training the same model; calibration and conformal quantiles downstream use OOF only. OOS touched once through the frozen JSON; the label variant used for the OOS table is fixed in advance (L1). Charges and slippage in the label so that the gate cannot win by cost avoidance alone; the kept-vs-skipped statistic is the selection criterion, never net.

238	### quant-ml-canon-feature-importance (priority 3)
239	
240	**technique.** Clustered feature importance (MDA and MDI on correlation clusters, single-feature importance per cluster) under purged cross-validation, the orthogonal-feature sanity check, fractional differentiation (fixed-width FFD with a hand-coded ADF choice of d*) as a candidate feature family, and TreeSHAP interaction values for discovering the 2-3-feature interactions that justify depth-2/3 rules.
241	
242	**what_it_answers.** Which of the 143 as-of columns (97 numeric, 114 pairs with |rho| > 0.9, so raw importances would be split by substitution) carry information about the intraday Foundation outcome; which at most 8 feature clusters the ST13/ST14 keys should be built from and what their config-expressible representative is; whether the canon's fractionally differentiated price features add anything beyond the ATR-normalised distances already in the table; which feature pairs interact strongly enough to justify a depth-2/3 rule, so that H5's rule search can be restricted (fewer trials, lower PBO).
243	
244	**method.** (1) Feature set: as-of numeric plus encoded categoricals as in the meta-label study; NaN kept for HGB, a missing-indicator plus median for bagging; columns with > 40% NaN dropped and listed. (2) FFD family: on log close per timeframe, fixed-width fractional differentiation for d in {0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0} with weight cut 1e-4 (window length recorded); ADF regression with constant and 2 lags hand-coded in numpy (MacKinnon 5% critical value -2.86 embedded and cited); d* = smallest d whose ADF statistic on IS bars is below the critical value; features at the SETUP bar: ffd_close_d*, its z-score against a 60-bar rolling std, the same on log volume; plus the CUSUM-filter counts from the regime study when available. (3) Clustering: Spearman correlation on IS, distance sqrt(0.5 (1 - rho)), scipy average linkage, cut chosen by silhouette in the 20-40 cluster range; every cluster gets a representative chosen by config-expressibility (integer counts and card fields before ATR ratios before raw points). (4) Model and protocol: BaggingClassifier of depth-limited trees on the L1 label with |net| weights under the harness splitter (12 purged, embargoed blocks). Clustered MDA: permute all features of a cluster jointly on the test fold, 5 permutations x 12 folds, record the drop in OOF weighted log-loss and, separately, the drop in OOF kept-vs-skipped expectancy at the fold's tau (the metric that matters); report mean and std across folds; a cluster is kept only when its mean MDA exceeds one std. MDI from the same forest summed per cluster; SFI: each cluster alone under the same CV. (5) Orthogonal check: PCA on standardised IS features, weighted Kendall tau between MDI rank and eigenvalue rank; a low tau is reported as a warning that the importance may be noise-fitting. (6) Interactions: xgboost max_depth 3, 200 rounds, eta 0.05 on the same folds restricted to the top-40 features; shap.TreeExplainer(...).shap_interaction_values on OOF rows; pairs ranked by mean |interaction|; the top 5 pairs with their split points from the tree structure become candidate depth-2/3 rules for H5 and the distillation step. (7) Stability: repeat (4) per IS year (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and report the rank correlation of cluster importances across years; a feature whose importance is not stable across years is not proposed as a key. Output: importance tables per timeframe, the shortlist (<= 8 clusters with representatives and definitions cited by README name), the FFD verdict, the interaction pairs.
245	
246	**leakage_controls.** As-of allowlist only (no fwd_*, fnd_*, fzpos_*, fzpost_*, final-state columns); fixed-width FFD is causal by construction and d* is chosen on IS bars only; clustering uses feature values only and is fitted on IS; MDA and SFI are computed on OOF predictions under purging and embargo (permutation on the test fold, model trained on the purged training folds); PCA fitted on IS; nothing is read from OOS; every model fit is logged in the harness ledger although this study proposes no gate itself.
247	
248	**compute.** FFD over 445k 1m bars x 10 d values with windows up to about 1,000 weights via numpy convolution: 1-2 minutes; ADF: 10 small regressions; clustering on 97 x 97: instant; MDA: 12 fits of a 300-tree bagging on <= 5k rows plus about 40 clusters x 5 permutations x 12 folds = 2,400 predict calls on <= 500 test rows: 5-8 minutes; xgboost and SHAP interactions on <= 5k rows x 40 features, depth 3: about 1 minute, interaction tensor 5k x 40 x 40 float64 = 64 MB (the full 100-feature tensor would be 400 MB, hence the top-40 restriction); total about 15 CPU-minutes per timeframe, peak under 500 MB.
249	
250	**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy (cluster.hierarchy linkage, stats.spearmanr, stats.weightedtau), sklearn (BaggingClassifier, DecisionTreeClassifier, PCA, HistGradientBoostingClassifier, metrics.silhouette_score), xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1; ADF and FFD hand-coded (statsmodels absent).
251	
252	**output_as_config.** A "features" object in the ST13/ST14 provenance: the ordered shortlist of at most 8 feature names with their README definitions, cluster membership and the per-year stability score; if FFD earns a cluster: {"ffd_d": d*, "ffd_window_bars": w, "ffd_weight_cut": 1e-4, "ffd_z_window": 60} as keys with source "learned:quant-ml-canon-feature-importance", otherwise the recorded verdict "FFD not adopted (clustered MDA <= 1 std)". Thresholds themselves come from the meta-label, sizing and H5 studies, not from here; this study fixes the vocabulary they may use.
253	
254	**novelty.** AFML (2018) ch. 5 (fractional differentiation, fixed-width FFD, the ADF-minimal d), ch. 8 (MDI, MDA, SFI, orthogonal features and the PCA-rank check); Lopez de Prado, Machine Learning for Asset Managers (2020) ch. 6 (clustered feature importance, the fix for substitution effects that the 2018 chapter did not have); Lundberg et al. (2020) TreeSHAP local explanations and interaction values, Nature Machine Intelligence. Current because clustered MDA plus SHAP interactions is the 2020s replacement for raw MDI rankings, and because it is the only principled way to shrink 143 columns to the 8 the lab's config format allows.

260	### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)
261	
262	**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.
263	
264	**what_it_answers.** The user's acceptance criterion made formal: can SETUPs be skipped with a finite-sample guarantee that at most alpha of the true winners are skipped (marginally over SETUPs, under exchangeability), what skip rate, loser recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy each alpha buys on IS out-of-fold, whether the winner coverage holds on OOS, what the hour-of-day guarantee costs in sample size, and how far a coverage-chosen threshold sits from the expectancy-chosen threshold of the meta-label study.
265	
266	**method.** Score s(x) = 1 - p_win_hat(x) taken from the meta-label study's IS out-of-fold probabilities (the scorecard variant, since the forest cannot live in the lab; the forest's scores are reported as reference). Cross-conformal / CV+ flavour: no separate calibration split is sacrificed (181 winners on 5m IS cannot afford one); within the harness's 12 purged folds, the conformal quantile is computed on the OOF scores of the winners in 11 folds and applied to the 12th, so the IS evaluation is itself out-of-fold. Mondrian by class: q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest OOF score among true winners; the prediction set contains 'win' iff s(x) <= q_alpha; gate = skip iff 'win' is not in the set, i.e. p_win_hat(x) < 1 - q_alpha. Guarantee: P(win in set | true winner) >= 1 - alpha, so at most alpha of winners are skipped in expectation; nothing is guaranteed for losers, their recall is measured. Alpha grid {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}; the smallest feasible alpha is 1/(n_win + 1) (0.0055 on 5m IS). Time taxonomy: class x time bin with three bins fixed in advance (09:15-10:29, 10:30-12:59, 13:00-15:19; the IS hour profile shows morning losses and afternoon gains); feasibility stated from winner counts per bin (5m IS: 16-39 winners per hour, so per-bin guarantees only for alpha >= 0.1; on 1m roughly 4-5x more). Robustness: |net|-weighted coverage (share of winners' gross net kept) reported next to count coverage, because the guarantee is per SETUP, not per rupee. Evaluation on IS-OOF per alpha: skip rate, winner coverage, loser recall, kept-vs-skipped expectancy and permutation p, control percentile (fz_report.random_control), top-decile-winner coverage; alpha chosen on IS by the pre-registered rule 'largest loser recall subject to winner coverage >= 0.9 and kept-vs-skipped difference > 0'. Exchangeability check: coverage per IS year and against the regime study's break tests. ACI variant (Gibbs and Candes): alpha_t+1 = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}, run sequentially over IS in time order, then continued into OOS from IS's final state without re-tuning, to see whether an online alpha keeps coverage under drift. OOS once: the frozen (alpha, taxonomy, thresholds) and the frozen ACI state, same table.
267	
268	**leakage_controls.** Scores are out-of-fold from the purged, embargoed splitter; the conformal quantile uses only winners from calibration folds; alpha, the time bins and the selection rule are fixed before OOS; ACI's state carries forward without any OOS tuning; the study reads no OOS row until the single frozen run; the comparison with the expectancy-chosen tau is on IS-OOF only.
269	
270	**compute.** Quantiles over <= 5k scores x 5 alphas x 12 folds and a sequential ACI loop over <= 5k rows: under 1 CPU-minute, under 100 MB; it depends only on the meta-label study's OOF file.
271	
272	**libraries.** numpy, pandas; mapie is not installed and not needed (split/cross-conformal quantile and ACI are about 40 lines); fz_report.random_control / permutation_p read-only.
273	
274	**output_as_config.** A "conformal" block in ST13/ST14: {"alpha": 0.10, "taxonomy": "class" or "class_x_timebin", "time_bins": [["09:15","10:29"],["10:30","12:59"],["13:00","15:19"]], "skip_if_score_below": s (per bin, the deployable scorecard's score at 1 - q_alpha), "calibration": {"n_winners": n, "is_window": "2021-10-01..2025-12-31", "oof_scores_sha": ...}, "aci": {"enabled": false or true, "gamma": 0.01, "alpha_state": a}}. The lab compares the scorecard score with a number; nothing else is code. Because the threshold is a single number per bin, it is the most compact form any gate in this study set can take.
275	
276	**novelty.** Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer (2005) Algorithmic Learning in a Random World; Mondrian conformal prediction (Vovk 2012); cross-conformal (Vovk 2015) and CV+ / jackknife+ (Barber, Candes, Ramdas and Tibshirani 2021, Annals of Statistics); Angelopoulos and Bates (2021) A gentle introduction to conformal prediction; Gibbs and Candes (2021) Adaptive Conformal Inference under distribution shift, NeurIPS. Current because conformal sets on top of a meta-labelling model are the 2021-2025 way to turn 'skip only losers' into a coverage statement with a finite-sample guarantee; it is not in AFML but is the natural successor to its bet-sizing chapter.
277	
278	**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: the guarantee is on winner count while P&L sits in the tail (a gate can keep 90% of winners and skip the three that made the year), exchangeability fails across the IS/OOS shift (5m -277 to -1,060), and the threshold it selects is the same number study 2 selects by expectancy, so it changes no trade. Fix: do not run as a study; report |net|-weighted coverage of the frozen gate as one row of study 2's OOS table; if a guarantee is ever wanted, weighted conformal on |net| with sessions as units.

280	**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: State the cross-conformal caveat: the OOF scores of the 11 calibration folds come from models that saw the 12th fold, so the finite-sample guarantee is the weaker CV+ / jackknife+ form (roughly 1 - 2 alpha), not 1 - alpha; report empirical OOF winner coverage per fold next to the nominal alpha. Merge with decision-making-4 into ONE operating-point step that reports both guarantees (winner coverage here, kept-loss risk there) on the same scorecard score, presents the Pareto front, and lets the user pick the point (Rule 0(c)); it is the same candidate as the scorecard for the OOS budget, not a second OOS look. Time-bin taxonomy only on 1m (5m has 16-39 winners per hour). Compute < 1 min.

282	### quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing (priority 5)
283	
284	**technique.** Probability calibration on purged out-of-fold predictions (isotonic and Platt, nested), expected-net sizing under the asymmetric payoff (Kelly fraction with class-conditional mean win and loss) discretised to 0-3 lots, compared with AFML's symmetric z-score sizing, judged with a lot-aware extension of the session-matched random control.
285	
286	**what_it_answers.** Given a calibrated p_win and the asymmetric payoff (5m IS: 22% winners, win mean +10,878 INR, loss mean -3,429 INR, top-decile winners 46% of gross wins), how many lots per SETUP, whether sizing adds expectancy per lot beyond the skip decision, whether the calibration is real (reliability curve, Brier skill against the 22% base rate, ECE) on IS-OOF and once on OOS, and whether the honest answer with 181 winners is simply 'one lot or skip'.
287	
288	**method.** Calibration: sklearn IsotonicRegression (and Platt via LogisticRegression as the low-variance alternative) fitted on the meta-label study's IS OOF p_hat against the L1 label, nested inside the harness splitter (fit on 11 folds' OOF, apply to the 12th); reliability curves in 5 quantile bins, Brier score and Brier skill score versus the base rate, expected calibration error, per model (scorecard is the deployable one). Conditional payoffs: W(x), L(x) = mean net of winners and of losers within calibrated-probability quintiles on the training folds; a HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='quantile' (0.5) on |net| is tried only if the importance study shows any feature predicts magnitude (prior: it does not; say so). Expected net e(x) = p_hat W - (1 - p_hat) L. Sizing rules compared: (a) AFML 10.3 for reference: m = 2 Phi(z) - 1 with z = (p_hat - 0.5) / sqrt(p_hat (1 - p_hat)), which is wrong at a 22% base rate and is shown to be so; (b) Kelly fraction f = p_hat / L_bar - (1 - p_hat) / W_bar, half-Kelly, mapped to lots by fixed bins; (c) expected-net bins: lots = 0 if e(x) < 0, 1 if e(x) < c1, 2 if e(x) < c2, else 3, with (c1, c2) on a coarse grid (multiples of the median cost, about 1,100 INR) chosen inside folds; every (c1, c2) tried goes to the harness ledger. Book: lots x the intraday Foundation net with charges recomputed per lot via lab.trade_charges (brokerage cap per order matters) and slippage per lot. Judgement: net per lot, kept-vs-skipped per lot, maximum drawdown and per-session Sharpe of the sized book versus the 1-lot gated book versus raw Foundation; lot-aware control: extend fz_report.random_control so each draw assigns the study's own multiset of lot sizes per session to randomly chosen Foundation positions of that session (seeded the same way), giving the percentile and p_beat of the sized book; block-bootstrap confidence intervals from the harness. Sample-size statement: two cut points learned on about 180 winners on 5m give wide intervals; if the CPCV 5th percentile of net-per-lot improvement is not above zero, the study's recommendation is 'lots = 1 or skip' and the size block carries that verdict. OOS once with the frozen calibration map and bins.
289	
290	**leakage_controls.** Calibration fitted on OOF predictions only and nested in the same purged, embargoed folds; W_bar, L_bar and the lot cut points from training folds only; no label information in x (as-of allowlist); the calibration map and bins are frozen with a sha before OOS; the lot-aware control uses the same seeding discipline as fz_report so the percentile reproduces; net per lot is the selection statistic so that adding lots to a few large winners cannot masquerade as skill without the control percentile agreeing.
291	
292	**compute.** Isotonic and Platt fits: milliseconds; sizing grid of about 20 (c1, c2) pairs x 12 folds: seconds; lot-aware random control 2,000 draws x 1,026 sessions vectorised in numpy: under 1 minute; peak under 100 MB.
293

## 7. The card

One row per bar, computed as of that bar and never rewritten. Fields: `zone_id` (the ref band), `visit_n`, `this_bars`, `this_vol`, `vol_na`, `first_bars`, `first_vol`, `first_vol_na`, `read`, `left_id` (the band whose LEAVE is live), `out_run`, `out_side`, `session_bar`, `gap_pts`, `wick_depth`, `last_hunt_at/dir`, `last_reject_at/dir`, `cluster_sit`, `prev_bars`, `prev_vol`, `last_leave_failed`, `in_id` (the band containing the close, nearest mid), `leave_side`, `leave_vol_ok`, `leave_kind`, `first_clock_lived`.

**Read precedence.** LEAVE (a LEAVE is live on `left_id`) → HUNT → REJECT → the inside read of the ref band's visit when the close is inside it → PENDING (the close is outside the ref band, visit still live) → NEW (no ref band).

**Inside reads.** Visit 1 reads FIRST_PRINT (`first_clock_lived` says whether it has lasted `accept_bars`). On a revisit, with B = the base visit (`volume_base`: the first visit, or the previous one): ACCEPTED when `this_bars ≥ accept_bars` and (volume is NA on either side, or `this_vol ≥ accept_vol_ratio × B.vol`); else THIN when volume is live and `this_vol < thin_ratio × B.vol`; else RECYCLE.

**Volume NA.** A bar is NA when its session is not the front month (`front_month == 0` in the 1-minute file) or its volume is 0. A visit is NA if any of its bars is; the first visit's NA flag never changes. NA makes ACCEPTED time-only, THIN unavailable, the HUNT burst skipped and R4 skipped. Because `fm_na` folds the front-month flag in, two visits with live volume are always in the same volume regime, so a cross-regime ratio cannot be computed by construction.

`leave_vol_ok` (the R4 of a LEAVE read): per-bar mean volume of the far-side closes since R1 ≥ the sit's per-bar mean; `null` when either side is NA; re-evaluated on every far-side bar.

---

## 8. The gate at a Foundation SETUP

Evaluated on the SETUP bar k with direction S, after the watch step of that bar. The ledger row is created first with the card's columns; on a LEAVE read it also records the entered band (`entered_zone_id`, `entered_visit_n`, `entered_read` = that band's read as if it were the ref band).

1. **A REENTER already decided on this bar** by the watch step (R5 satisfied on the SETUP bar itself) makes the row `REENTER` with branch `watch`.
2. **Hard BLOCK**, in this order, no watch opened and any existing watch untouched: `in_position` (an FZ position is open on this bar), `clock` (bar open time ≥ `no_entry_from`), `open_pierce` (within the session's first `open_bars` bars and before `open_window_until`, the bar's range crosses an edge of a band whose last visit ended in an earlier session and that has fewer than `open_sit_closes` closes inside today), `hunt_fade` (the latest HUNT of the ref band or of the band just left, or of any band under `fade_scope = any_band`, is in S's direction, completed within `fade_block_bars`, same session), `new` (the read is NEW).
3. **TAKE branches**, the first that holds:
   - **leave**: read LEAVE, S equals the leave side, `leave_vol_ok` is not False, not a gap LEAVE inside the first `open_quiet_bars` bars, and `leave_far_side`: `any` accepts; `block_list` refuses when the entered band reads RECYCLE, THIN, HUNT or REJECT (`block_reason = leave_into_recycle`); `no_band` refuses whenever a band contains the close (`leave_into_band`). A refusal records `take_why` and falls through to WATCH.
   - **first_print**: read FIRST_PRINT, the visit is at least `first_print_min_bars` old, S equals the visit's `entry_dir`.
   - **defend**: read ACCEPTED and the ref band's latest HUNT or latest REJECT (one slot each, §6) fell in this visit, within `defend_window_bars`, at the edge S points away from.
   - A **leave** TAKE of the band a watch waits on, in the watch's direction, is that watch's REENTER instead (branch `leave`, `reenter_reason = take_on_watch:leave`); a first_print or defend TAKE stays Foundation's own position and leaves the watch as it is.
   - A TAKE calls `open_position('TAKE')`; the engine may have skipped the SETUP for a wrong-side stop, in which case the row records `refused` and no position opens. An opposite-direction TAKE ends an open watch (`opposite_take`). A converted (branch-1) REENTER that the callback refuses keeps `gate = REENTER` with `refused` set and no position, and its `outcome_gate` is then REENTER too; this has not occurred on the tape (0 rows in all four strategies), and what it should become is open (S44 b).
4. **WATCH_EDGE**: `edge_watch = ref_band`, the read is PENDING, the previous close was inside the ref band and S is the side the close is on: a watch on the ref band that is already armed (this bar is R1).
5. **WATCH**: a band contains the close: a watch on that band with `dir = S`, not armed.
6. **BLOCK `new`** otherwise.

One watch at a time: a later SETUP that opens a watch replaces the current one (`outcome = replaced`); a BLOCKed SETUP leaves it untouched. `gate` on the row is the decision as of the SETUP bar (what the truncation test compares); `outcome_gate` is how the SETUP ended (REENTER when a later REENTER used this SETUP as its R5), and the tables and headline counts use `outcome_gate`.

---

## 9. The watch machine

A watch pins a snapshot of its band (edges, mid, the sit's per-bar mean volume) and runs once per bar before the gate, from the bar after it opened.

- **Cancels**, checked first: the first bar of a new session (`session_end`); `leave_closes` consecutive closes beyond the band on the side opposite to the watch direction (`opposite_leave`); from ARMED, `cancel_inside_bars` consecutive closes back inside (`back_inside`). An opposite TAKE cancels from the gate (`opposite_take`).
- **R1**: a close beyond the band on the watch's side arms the watch (`armed_at`; `first_armed_at` on the first arming). A close back inside breaks the far-side run; the next far-side close arms again (R1 again), so R3 (no close inside or across the mid since R1) holds by construction on the unbroken run. The ledger reports both `armed_bars` (from the first arming) and `rearmed_bars` (from the latest).
- **R2**: `leave_closes` consecutive far-side closes. **R4**: per-bar mean volume of the far-side run ≥ the pinned sit mean, skipped (None) when the run or the sit is volume-NA. `r4_bars_evaluated / fail / na` are counted per window.
- **R5**: a Foundation SETUP in the watch direction on this bar or on the previous bar of the same session.
- **REENTER** on the first bar j where R1–R5 hold, unless the bar's open time is at or past `no_entry_from` (`clock_1520` counted, watch stays armed) or a position is open (`reenter_in_position`). The callback prices nothing back; it may refuse (`wrong_side_stop`, `sl_dead_at_fill`), counted as `reenter_refused`, the watch continues. On success the row of the R5 SETUP gets `fill_bar`, `fill_used` (`setup_close` when j is the SETUP bar, else `reenter_close`), `fill_delay_bars`, `edge_dist_pts`, `armed_bars`, `rearmed_bars`, `reenter_reason` and `outcome_gate = REENTER`.
- **Outcomes** in the watch log: `reenter`, `replaced`, `cancelled:<reason>` (never armed) or `armed_expired:<reason>` (armed), `active` at the data end. `no_same_dir_setup` counts armed watches that expired with R1–R4 satisfied on their last bar.

Position lifetime is entry bar ≤ k < exit bar, so a SETUP on a position's exit bar may open a new one at that bar's close; `build_trades` asserts that no two FZ positions overlap under that convention.

---

## 10. Execution: `fz_exec.py`

## 19. v2: rooms (Strategies 7, 8)

**Why.** The user's verdict on the base (2026-09-27): the card named tiles, not rooms. Zones were born at every protected level and every cluster sit, absorbed into a permanent 20-point mesh and never retired, so on 3 Sep the card said `B07-23 14:52 visit 7` (and `B07-02 10:31 visit 51` elsewhere) where the user saw one afternoon box; every LEAVE was a step from tile A into tile B; the first clock was a July sit, so the volume ratio was NA on the only window with volume; REENTER fired on tile edges. Median visit_n at a 1m SETUP was 19, FIRST_PRINT at SETUP 0, and the gate sat at the 6th percentile of its random control (S39). v2 changes identity only: what a room is, when it is born, when it dies, what it is called. Reads, precedence, PENDING, LEAVE liveness, REJECT, the gate's order and branches, `leave_far_side`, the watch machine, `fz_exec` and `fz_report` are the same code. Recorded as S42 in `docs/STRATEGY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`.

**Room model** (`room_model = "rooms"`, in `fz.py` next to the band model; `bands` is the base):

1. **Birth only from sits.** A room is born on the transition into a sit (the last `cluster_bars` closes of one session within `cluster_width`), centred on the sit's `(max + min) / 2`, ± `band_half_width`, origin = the sit's first bar; visit 1 is that sit, replayed over the window only. No drift births (`drift_birth = false`) and no swing births (`birth_a_source = "none"`; `protected_level` / `every_swing` still work in either model, as diagnostics).
2. **No mesh.** A sit overlapping a live room by at least `merge_overlap` of the width (with 0.5: its mid is inside the room) is a visit of that room, never a birth; it takes the live visit when its close is inside that room (below). Two live rooms never overlap (a shared edge is allowed). A sit that overlaps live rooms by less than `merge_overlap` is a new room, and `room_overlap` says how the overlap is removed: **`supersede`** (seeded): the new room keeps its full width and the rooms it overlaps are retired on its birth bar (`retired_by = superseded`); `clip`: the new room's edges stop at the neighbours' edges. Retired rooms absorb nothing and contain no price.
3. **Rooms retire.** On a session's first bar, a room with no inside close in the last `room_max_age_sessions` sessions (`session - last session with an inside close > room_max_age_sessions`) is retired (`retired_by = retired`), unless it holds the live visit. A new sit at a retired room's price is a new room with a new name and its own first clock. A LEAVE still live on a room that retires ends (`leave_end_retired`).
4. **Names.** `zone_id = "<letter> <mm-dd hh:mm>"`: the letter is the room's birth order within its birth session (A … Z, then AA, AB …), the time its birth bar. Rooms keep `kind = "B"` (sit-born; `A` only under a swing `birth_a_source`), so the Zone-gate tab's zone-kind table and the chart colours work unchanged.
5. **Visits and touches.** A stay with fewer than `visit_min_bars` inside closes that ends by the leave rule is a *touch*: it keeps its record (`touch: true`), does not advance `visit_n`, and is counted on the room and on the card (`touches`). Visit numbers are as-of: the current stay counts as a visit while it lasts. The first visit (`first_bars`, `first_vol`) and the previous visit (`volume_base = previous`, `prev_bars`) are the first / previous stay that is not a touch. With `visit_min_bars = 1` no stay can be a touch (a stay opens on an inside close), which is how the base stays unchanged.
6. **The live visit follows the sit.** When a room is born, or a sit is absorbed by a live room, while another room holds the live visit and the sit's close is inside the new (or absorbing) room, the old visit ends at the previous bar (`ended_by = sit_moved`, no LEAVE is recorded) and the room the market sits in takes the visit (the base instead cuts the newborn zone's replayed visit, `ref_live`). A room retired by supersession while it holds the visit with no room taking over ends its visit with `ended_by = superseded`.
7. **Leave and hunt.** `leave_closes` 1m 3, 5m 2 (so HUNT and LEAVE do not overlap on 1m). The close-form HUNT is `1 ≤ outside run ≤ hunt_max_bars` closes on one side, then a close back inside (the base only ever had a run of 1); the burst test takes the loudest of those outside bars and is skipped when any of them is volume-NA (identical to the base for a run of 1). The 5m wick form is unchanged.

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
